scenarios.title: {J} Left Out Again: Talks With {M}?
scenarios.text: The squad list goes up and {J}'s name isn't on it again. In the corridor, {M} walks past without stopping. The door to his office is open. It feels like an invitation, or a dare.

choices.label: Knock on his door
choices.desc: Ask directly what you need to change.
choices.hint: Could clear the air — or confirm the worst.

out.text: Forty minutes in {M}'s office. Honest, uncomfortable, useful. He gives {J} three things to fix and a sliver of hope.
“I pick the team I think wins.” That's it. {J} leaves knowing less than when he went in.

choices.label: Work in silence
choices.text: {J} is first in, last out for a week. Nobody says anything. Somebody notices.

choices.label: Ask your agent to call
choices.desc: Make it clear you'll leave if needed.
choices.hint: Agitating for a transfer damages trust.
choices.text: The agent makes the call. Within a day the dressing room knows. {M} now has a reason.

scenarios.title: {M}: “{J} Is the Model Professional”
scenarios.text: Asked about his squad in the pre-match press conference, {M} goes out of his way to mention {J}: “He trains like he's never played a game. I wish I had ten like him.” The quote is everywhere by the evening.

scenarios.title: Half-Time Hairdryer: {M} Singles Out {J}
scenarios.text: At half-time {M} kicks a water bottle across the dressing room and points at {J}: “You. Where were you for their goal? Asleep?” Twenty-five players stare at the floor.
scenarios.prompt: Everyone is waiting to see what you do.

choices.label: Take it
choices.desc: Nod. Say nothing. Respond on the pitch.
choices.text: {J} nods once. The second half is his best forty-five minutes of the season.

choices.label: Answer back
choices.desc: “I was covering for someone else's mistake.”
choices.hint: True or not, this is a power struggle.

out.text: Silence. Then {M} sits down. “Then cover better.” Strangely, he respects it.
{M} subs {J} off at half-time, in front of everyone. The message is clear.

scenarios.title: {M} Wants {J} at Wing-Back
scenarios.text: Injuries at the back. {M} calls {J} into his office: “I need someone with legs on the right. Wing-back. Just for a few weeks.” Everyone knows “a few weeks” in football can mean forever.

choices.label: Accept for the team
choices.hint: Trust up; your attacking numbers suffer.
choices.text: {J} plays wing-back for a month. He learns to defend. {M} learns he's a team player.

choices.label: Politely decline
choices.desc: Explain you'll help more in your position.
choices.hint: Refusing a tactical role badly damages trust.
choices.text: {M} listens, says “fine”, and doesn't pick {J} at all that weekend.

scenarios.title: {M} Sacked: A New Manager Arrives
scenarios.text: The board loses patience on a Tuesday morning. By the afternoon, {M}'s office is empty and a new manager is introduced at a press conference: different ideas, different favourites. Every player starts from zero.
scenarios.prompt: How do you approach the new manager?

choices.label: Introduce yourself first
choices.desc: Be the first to knock on his door.
choices.text: {J} is first through the door. The new manager writes his name at the top of a fresh notebook.

choices.label: Impress in training
choices.text: {J} trains like it's a trial. In a sense, it is.

choices.label: Defend the old manager publicly
choices.desc: Loyalty to the man who gave you a chance.
choices.hint: Admirable. The new man may not like it.
choices.text: {J} praises the sacked manager in an interview. Fans love the loyalty. The new manager reads it too.

scenarios.title: Dropped for the Big Game
scenarios.text: The biggest match of the month, and {J} sees his name on the bench list. {M} explains in two sentences: a tactical decision, the opponent's left-back, nothing personal. It feels personal.

choices.label: Accept it professionally
choices.desc: Support the team from the bench.
choices.text: {J} warms up longer than anyone and cheers every tackle. {M} notices.

choices.label: Sulk
choices.text: {J} sits at the end of the bench with his hood up. The photographers capture it beautifully.

scenarios.title: Man-Marking Assignment: Stop Their Star
scenarios.text: {M} has a special job for {J} this week: follow the opposition's best player everywhere. Toilet breaks included, he jokes. It means sacrificing your own game completely.

ok.text: The star touches the ball eleven times. {M} hugs {J} at the final whistle. The newspapers don't mention him.

bad.text: The star ghosts away from {J} twice and scores once. {M} sighs. “At least you tried.”

choices.label: Ask to play your own game
choices.desc: You can hurt them in attack.
choices.text: {M} doesn't argue; he just picks someone else for the job, and for the team.

scenarios.title: {M} Wants to Tie {J} Down
scenarios.text: {M} catches {J} after training: “I've told the board I want you here long-term. Don't let your agent make it complicated.”

scenarios.title: Late for the Tactical Meeting
scenarios.text: {J}'s alarm didn't go off. He arrives at the tactical meeting nine minutes late, hair still wet. {M} stops talking mid-sentence and waits for him to sit down. The silence is deafening.

choices.label: Apologise and accept the fine
choices.text: “Sorry, boss. No excuse.” {M} nods. The fine is posted that afternoon.

out.text: The excuse works. {J} feels sick about it all afternoon.
A teammate saw him leaving his apartment at 9:40. The excuse becomes a lie, publicly.

scenarios.title: Teammates Whisper: “Manager's Favourite”
scenarios.text: {J} plays every week, even after bad games. The whispers have started: teacher's pet, coach's son, untouchable. {T} says it out loud in the gym.

choices.label: Prove it's merit
choices.desc: Work twice as hard in training.
choices.text: {J} wins every drill for two weeks. The whispers die.

out.text: {T} backs down. “Just joking, bro.” He wasn't.
Shouting, shoving, staff stepping in. {M} has to decide whose side he's on in public.

scenarios.title: {M} Notices Something Is Wrong
scenarios.text: {M} calls {J} into his office, but not to talk about football. “Your head isn't here. What's going on at home?”

choices.label: Tell him everything
choices.hint: Managers are people too. Most of them.
choices.text: {M} listens, then gives {J} three days off to go home. “Football will be here when you come back.”

choices.label: “Everything's fine”
choices.text: {M} doesn't believe him, but lets it go. “My door is open.”

scenarios.title: {M}: “Young Players Must Wait Their Turn”
scenarios.text: In a press conference, {M} is asked why the club's young players don't play. His answer: “Young players must earn it. Nobody is given anything here.” He doesn't mention {J} by name. He doesn't need to.
scenarios.prompt: Supporters are campaigning online for you to play.

choices.label: Share the campaign
choices.desc: Let the fans speak for you.
choices.hint: Public pressure on a manager rarely ends well.
choices.text: {J} shares a fan post demanding he plays. {M} sees it within the hour. The temperature drops.

choices.label: Ask fans to support the team
choices.text: {J} posts: “Support the team. My chance will come.” {M} reads it. His next press conference is warmer.

scenarios.title: The Assistant Coach Becomes {J}'s Advocate
scenarios.text: The assistant coach has been watching {J} closely. In staff meetings he's started saying his name. He tells {J} privately: “Keep doing what you're doing. I'm talking you up.”

scenarios.title: {M} Switches to a Back Three
scenarios.text: {M} changes the formation to a back three with wing-backs. Some players benefit. Some lose their place entirely. In the new system, {J}'s role is unclear.

choices.label: Study the new system
choices.text: {J} learns the new system faster than anyone. {M} uses him to explain it to others.

choices.label: Wait and see
choices.text: {J} waits. The system stays. He's a step behind for a month.

scenarios.title: {M} on the Brink: “Play for Me This Weekend”
scenarios.text: The press says {M} has one match to save his job. In the final team meeting, he doesn't talk about tactics. He looks at the squad and says, quietly: “Whatever happens Saturday, thank you.” Several players look at the floor.
scenarios.prompt: The captain says the team should play for the manager.

choices.label: Rally the team
choices.text: {J} speaks up: “We owe him.” The team plays like a team possessed.

choices.label: Stay neutral
choices.text: {J} keeps his head down. If the manager goes, the next one needs to see a professional.

scenarios.title: One-to-One Review With {M}
scenarios.text: Every month {M} reviews each player one-to-one: clips, data, a short conversation. Today he puts {J}'s heatmap on the screen. “Tell me what you see.”

choices.label: Honest self-criticism
choices.desc: Point out your own mistakes first.
choices.text: {J} identifies three mistakes before {M} can. The manager closes the laptop. “Good. That's what I wanted.”

out.text: {M} likes the confidence. “Good. Believe it.”
{M} clicks to the next clip: a mistake. Then another. “Still good?”

scenarios.title: {J} Is Running on Empty
scenarios.text: The legs are gone. {J} has played every minute of the last eight matches. The data says he's at risk. {M} needs him on Saturday.

choices.label: Ask for rest
choices.desc: Better to miss one game than six.
choices.hint: Some managers see it as weakness.

out.text: {M} looks at the data and agrees. {J} watches from the stands and returns refreshed.
{M} agrees, but his replacement plays well. Now {J} has to win his place back.
{J} plays. He's tired, but he gets through it. {M} notices the sacrifice.
Seventieth minute: the hamstring goes. Exactly what the data predicted.

scenarios.title: Disciplinary Hearing: {J} Accused of Breaking Curfew
scenarios.text: A hotel staff member reported a player leaving the team hotel after curfew on the last away trip. The CCTV is blurry. {M} thinks it was {J}.

out.text: The footage shows {T}, not {J}. {M} apologises, almost.
The footage is inconclusive. {M} keeps his suspicion. {J} keeps his anger.

choices.label: Take the blame for a teammate
choices.text: {J} takes the fine to protect {T}. {T} finds out and becomes his most loyal friend in the squad.

scenarios.title: {M} Tells {J} About His Own Career
scenarios.text: On a long away trip, {M} sits next to {J} on the bus. He talks about his own playing career: the injury at twenty-four, the clubs that didn't want him, the year he worked in his father's shop. “Talent is common,” he says. “Patience isn't.”

scenarios.title: {M} Names the New Penalty Taker
scenarios.text: The regular penalty taker missed two in a row. {M} holds a penalty competition in training: five each, the goalkeepers trying everything to put people off.

choices.label: Same corner every time
choices.desc: Hit it hard and low, bottom left.

ok.text: Five out of five. {M} points at {J}. “Yours.”

bad.text: The keeper reads the third one and gloats. Someone else wins.

choices.label: Wait for the keeper to move

ok.text: Five out of five, each one rolled in as the keeper dived. Cold-blooded. The job is his.

bad.text: The keeper stands still on the second one and catches it. Laughter.

scenarios.title: {M} Leaves for a Bigger Club — and Wants {J} to Follow
scenarios.text: {M} has been offered a job at a bigger club. On his last day, he takes {J} aside: “I'll be calling your agent in the summer. Be ready.” Then he's gone, and a new manager is introduced.

scenarios.title: Tactical Meetings in a Language {J} Barely Speaks
scenarios.text: {M}'s team talks are fast, full of slang and in a language {J} is still learning. He understands about sixty percent. Today he missed an instruction about corners and the team conceded from one.

choices.label: Ask for a translator in meetings
choices.text: The club arranges a translator for meetings. {J} catches up, but feels like a guest.

choices.label: Private language lessons
choices.text: {J} pays {cost} for intensive lessons. Two months later, he makes a joke in a team meeting and the whole room laughs. He belongs.

scenarios.title: {M} Blames the Players Publicly
scenarios.text: After the defeat, {M} tells the press: “Some players don't care enough about this badge.” He doesn't name names. Journalists start guessing. {J}'s name comes up on talk radio.

out.text: “Not you. You care.” {J} leaves relieved.
{M} pauses a long time. “If you have to ask…”

choices.label: Respond on the pitch
choices.text: In the next match, {J} covers more ground than anyone on the pitch. The talk radio moves on.

scenarios.title: {M} Suggests a Loan
scenarios.text: {M} is honest: “You're not going to play here this season. A loan would be good for you. Think about it.” He says it kindly. It still feels like being shown the door.

choices.label: Ask the agent to find one
choices.text: {J} agrees. The club makes it known he's available for loan.

choices.label: Fight for your place
choices.text: “I'll fight for it.” {M} shrugs. “Good. Show me.”

scenarios.title: A Board Member Wants {J} in the Team
scenarios.text: A powerful board member, also a businessman and local politician, has taken a liking to {J}. He calls {M} to suggest {J} should play more. {M} hates interference. Everyone at the club knows about the call.
scenarios.prompt: The board member invites you to dinner.

choices.label: Accept the dinner
choices.hint: The manager will see it as betrayal.
choices.text: A long dinner at an expensive restaurant. The board member promises to “take care of things”. {M} finds out the next day.

choices.label: Decline politely
choices.text: {J} declines politely. {M} hears about it, and something in his manner toward {J} warms.

scenarios.title: A Niggle Before the Big Match
scenarios.text: {J}'s groin has been tight all week. Nothing serious, probably. If he tells the medical team, they'll rest him for the biggest match of the month. If he doesn't, he plays.

choices.label: Tell them
choices.hint: Safe body. Might lose your place.
choices.text: The physio rests him for the match. The replacement plays okay. {M} appreciates the honesty.

choices.label: Hide it
choices.hint: Might be fine. Might be a long injury.

out.text: The groin holds. Nobody ever knows.
Twenty minutes in, the groin goes. A moderate tear. The medical team is furious.

scenarios.title: {M} Offers {J} the Captaincy
scenarios.text: The captain is leaving. {M} calls {J} into his office and puts the armband on the desk between them. “The players respect you. I trust you. It's yours if you want it.”

choices.label: Accept
choices.text: {J} accepts. The first time he leads the team out, his mother is in the stand holding a phone above her head with shaking hands.

choices.label: Decline
choices.text: {J} thanks him and declines. {M} respects the honesty and gives it to someone else.

scenarios.title: The Board Member's Favour Comes Due
scenarios.text: The board member who “took care of things” calls. His nephew is a footballer looking for a trial. Would {J} speak to {M}?

choices.label: Speak to {M}
choices.hint: The manager will not like this.
choices.text: {M} listens with a face like stone. The nephew gets a trial. {J} loses something with {M} that won't come back easily.

choices.label: Refuse
choices.text: {J} says no. The board member hangs up without saying goodbye. Contract talks next year may be colder.

scenarios.title: Old Manager Calls: “Come and Play for Me”
scenarios.text: {J}'s former manager calls from his new club. He wants {J} to join him: same system, bigger stage. His agent says the clubs are talking.

scenarios.title: {M} Gives {J} Extra Tactical Lessons
scenarios.text: {M} has noticed {J} is often out of position. Instead of dropping him, he invites {J} to his office every Thursday with coffee and a tablet full of clips.

scenarios.title: Rotation: {M} Explains the Plan
scenarios.text: {M} gathers the rotation players. “You will all play. Not every week. Be ready when it's your turn.” Half the room nods. Half hears “not every week”.

choices.label: Stay ready
choices.text: {J} treats every training session like an audition. When his chance comes, he's sharp.

choices.label: Push for more
choices.text: {J} tells {M} he wants to start every week. {M} says, “Then be undroppable.”

scenarios.title: {M} Gives {J} a Book
scenarios.text: {M} leaves a book on {J}'s peg: a biography of a legendary player from another era, with one passage underlined in pencil. No note. Just the line.

scenarios.title: Shouting Match in the Corridor
scenarios.text: It starts with a question about minutes and ends with {J} and {M} shouting in the corridor outside the dressing room. Players poke their heads out of doors. The kit man pretends to count socks.

choices.label: Walk away
choices.text: {J} walks away mid-sentence. It isn't over, but it isn't worse.

choices.label: Apologise the next day
choices.text: {J} knocks on the door the next morning. {M} accepts the apology without looking up.

choices.label: Say you want to leave
choices.text: “Sell me then.” {M}: “Gladly.” By the afternoon, {J} is transfer listed.
